title: [US] train_s2: shape, null rates, length distribution
headline: US train_s2 is 3,016,817 rows (59.9215% of the 5,034,616-row file) and is clean on every integrity axis: name_empty=0, prefix_bad=0, len_hist sums exactly to rows. New finding: has_comma (2,905,696) equals rows-addr_empty (3,016,817-111,121) EXACTLY, so 100.00% of non-empty US addresses contain a comma and has_comma is fully redundant with addr_empty for US. The invariant holds in all 6 US slices and breaks only on 333 France + 3 India test rows.

lengths.num_digits_scope: address only (build_profile.py:114 uses ba, not bn)

new_finding.statement: In US train_s2, has_comma (2,905,696) == rows - addr_empty (3,016,817 - 111,121 = 2,905,696) exactly. Since no empty string can contain a comma, this proves 100.00% of non-empty US addresses contain at least one comma.

cross_slice_test.note: deficit = (rows - addr_empty) - has_comma; 0 means every non-empty address has a comma
cross_slice_test.verdict: Invariant is exact for every US slice in the whole dataset. Broken only by 180+153 France and 2+1 India test rows.

new_finding.implication: has_comma is a redundant feature for US - it is an exact alias of address-emptiness and carries no additional discriminative information. Any downstream feature or quality gate keyed on 'address contains a comma' should be audited. NOT confirmed as an actual defect: I did not search the feature builder.

statistical_power.note: All rates pinned to within +/-0.04 percentage points; rarest measured feature (dig6) still has 42,026 supporting rows.

consistency_checks.check: exact mean name_chars/rows within bucket-implied range

already_checked_disposition.REFUTED-1_french_postal_pin: NOT re-derived. My data is consistent with the refutation: US dig5/row = 0.107 in this slice, i.e. US rows are rich in 5-digit numbers, the opposite of France. No support for REFUTED-1 found.
already_checked_disposition.REFUTED-2_fr_regions_too_thin: NOT re-derived and cannot be tested here: the profile collects no state/region/city field at all. No evidence either way.

gaps: No per-component address structure (component count, order, or which component holds city/state/ZIP). Biggest gap; blocks direct testing of the French component-order question.
No state/region/city fields collected, so REFUTED-2 is untestable from the profile.
No pin field; cannot separate US ZIP+4 dig6 runs from Indian PINs per-row.
Builder strips before testing emptiness, so true-empty and whitespace-only cannot be distinguished.
name_tokens is capped at top-4000 and hapax-pruned, so no vocabulary size, TTR, or unique-business counts. The 3,681 short tokens counted are a LOWER BOUND for the 91,611 short-name rows.

recommendations.action: Do NOT add null-handling or prefix-repair logic for US.
recommendations.rationale: name_empty=0 and prefix_bad=0 exactly; S2- prefix is a valid zero-defect partition key.
recommendations.expected_effect: none - recommendation is to avoid wasted effort

recommendations.action: Audit for and drop any feature gated on has_comma for the US path, or document it as an alias of address-emptiness.
recommendations.rationale: provably redundant on 100% of US rows across train and test.
recommendations.expected_effect: no US accuracy change; removes a feature that would mis-generalise if the invariant broke

recommendations.action: No dictionary change warranted from this slice.
recommendations.rationale: no normalisation gap measured; no CONFIRMED/LIKELY/SPECULATIVE entries proposed

recommendations.action: Collect per-component address structure for France (component count, per-component digit/alpha flags, index of component containing a 5-/6-digit number).
recommendations.rationale: would settle the component-order question and close the largest blind spot in the profile
recommendations.expected_effect: enables the untested French component-order analysis
